On this page

Core components ​

The core:: namespace holds the components the format itself relies on: naming, placement, hierarchy and types. Every other component is ordinary data that Mosaic carries without interpreting.

Their schemas live in sdk/ts/src/core/schemas/.

TypeHas a valueWhat it does
core::nameno, the name is the reference idA human-readable name for the node
core::childno, the child's node id is the reference idHangs a node beneath this one
core::inheritno, the parent type's node id is the reference idMakes this node be another
core::transformyes, one row in core::transform.ndjsonThe node's local placement

Value-less components ​

Three of the four carry no row at all. Their reference leaves out index (it defaults to -1), and the reference id, which every reference has anyway, is the data:

json
{ "type": "core::name",    "id": "Left plinth" }
{ "type": "core::child",   "id": "d6c1d2ba-9376-4461-8c56-27c496c1d2ba" }
{ "type": "core::inherit", "id": "70000000-7000-4000-8000-700000000001" }

So a node can carry many of each, one per name, child or type, and a later section can drop exactly one of them with a DELETE on that id:

json
{ "type": "core::child", "id": "d6c1d2ba-9376-4461-8c56-27c496c1d2ba", "operation": "DELETE" }

It also means names, hierarchy and types can be read straight off the references, without touching a single component table. That is what lets the viewer draw a tree of a whole building without loading its geometry.

core::name ​

A human-readable name for the node. A converted glTF or IFC node keeps the name a person would recognise this way, next to the uuid the node is identified by. A node may carry several names.

core::child ​

A parent-child link. The reference id is the id of the child node.

  • One node can hold many children.
  • A node that is someone's child is not a root of the scene.
  • Naming the same node from several parents places it several times. The copies share their mesh, so the geometry is stored once however often it appears, and a placed node brings its whole subtree along.
  • A link may cross an import: a scene can place a node that lives in another archive.
  • Links that would expand forever are refused. A cycle is reported with the path that closes it.

core::inherit ​

An is-a link. The reference id is the id of the node to inherit from.

When composing, the node receives every component of the node it inherits from, except where it carries one under the same reference id. Its own always wins. So a type node can hold the mesh once, and every node that is-a that type picks it up while overriding only its transform.

  • A node may inherit from several nodes. Where two offer the same id, the one named first wins.
  • Chains are allowed: a node that inherits from a node that inherits from a third gets all three, with the nearest winning.
  • The is-a links themselves come along, so a node two steps down a chain still answers to the type at the top. "Everything that is a Chair" is a question about nodes, not a graph walk.
  • Unlike core::child, this changes the node itself, not what hangs beneath it.
  • Inheritance is expanded only when composing. The file always records what was written.

See The format for a worked example.

core::transform ​

The local transform of a node, either as translation / rotation / scale or as a 4×4 column-major matrix. The field names and defaults follow the glTF 2.0 node, but a transform is not specific to glTF, which is why it lives in core.

FieldTypeDefault
translation[x, y, z][0, 0, 0]
rotationunit quaternion [x, y, z, w][0, 0, 0, 1]
scale[x, y, z][1, 1, 1]
matrix16 numbers, column-majoridentity
json
{"translation":[0,2,0],"scale":[0.5,0.5,0.5]}
{"translation":[-1,0,0]}

Composing writes it straight onto the glTF node, as a matrix or as TRS.
